last-2-versions.title: Last 2 versions of the evergreen engines

rules.title: iframe has no accessible name
rules.why: A frame without a name is announced as an unnamed frame, so a screen-reader user cannot tell what it contains before entering it.
rules.detectionHint: An iframe start tag whose attribute list contains none of title, aria-label or aria-labelledby.
falsePositives: A decorative frame that sets aria-hidden="true" on itself and holds no interactive content
A frame whose accessible name is supplied by a wrapper component that spreads the attribute at runtime

migration.notes: The title must describe the frame's content; it cannot be generated automatically.

rules.title: javascript: URL in a link or source
rules.why: A javascript: URL executes script in the page's origin, is blocked by a Content-Security-Policy that forbids inline script, and is an injection sink whenever the value is not fully trusted.
rules.detectionHint: An href or src value (quoted HTML attribute or JSX string literal) whose scheme is javascript:.
falsePositives: The literal appears inside a comment or a documentation string
A test asserts that such a value is rejected

migration.notes: When the element genuinely navigates, use a real URL; when it performs an action, use a button.

rules.title: img has no intrinsic dimensions
rules.why: Without width and height the browser cannot reserve space before the image loads, so content jumps and the layout shift is charged to the page.
rules.detectionHint: An img element with neither width nor height, in a file where no aspect-ratio is visible, and which is not a framework image component that reserves space itself.
falsePositives: The image is rendered by next/image with fill, which requires absolute positioning and supplies its own sizing contract
The dimensions arrive through a design-system wrapper component rather than the tag
A stylesheet sets aspect-ratio for this element's class

migration.notes: Add the real intrinsic ratio; CSS can still size the rendered box.

rules.title: viewport blocks pinch zoom
rules.why: Blocking zoom removes the only way a low-vision user can enlarge text on a phone, and no content benefits from it.
rules.detectionHint: A viewport meta tag containing user-scalable=no, or maximum-scale set below 5.
falsePositives: A maximum-scale value of 5 or greater, which does not meaningfully restrict zoom
The pattern appears in a template that is never served (documentation, a test fixture)

rules.title: Large motion ignores prefers-reduced-motion
rules.why: Motion sickness is a real vestibular response; a blanket animation that ignores the user's stated preference can make a page unusable for them.
rules.detectionHint: Two or more transform or animation declarations in a file that has no prefers-reduced-motion media block.
falsePositives: Motion is limited to a short opacity fade, which is not a vestibular trigger
The reduced-motion guard lives in a shared stylesheet outside the scanned paths
The motion is a canvas or video background the author cannot express in CSS

rules.title: autocomplete disabled on a credential field
rules.why: Browsers do not stop password managers because of autocomplete=off, so the attribute buys nothing while blocking the helpful autofill path and the correct field-purpose metadata.
rules.detectionHint: An input with autocomplete="off" whose type is password, or whose name or id suggests a credential field.
falsePositives: A genuinely one-time value that must not be stored, such as an OTP, where autocomplete="one-time-code" is the better answer than off
A search field, where off is a legitimate preference

migration.notes: Use current-password or new-password so the browser offers the right behaviour.

rules.title: @ts-ignore instead of @ts-expect-error
rules.why: @ts-expect-error fails when the error disappears, so the suppression removes itself; @ts-ignore silently outlives the bug it was hiding.
falsePositives: The suppression targets a line that will never produce an error by design (for example a generated declaration file). The rule still reports it; use a reasoned decision record to suppress the finding.

migration.after: // @ts-expect-error -- value is populated by the loader above
